questions.stem: The wooden stand that holds a canvas upright while an artist paints is the
questions.explanation: An easel supports the canvas or board at a convenient working height and angle.

questions.stem: A thin flexible steel blade with a cranked handle, used to mix paint and apply it thickly, is a
questions.explanation: The palette knife mixes colours and can lay on thick paint.

questions.stem: A design in which the left half is a mirror image of the right half shows
questions.explanation: Symmetrical balance places equal elements on each side of a central axis.

questions.stem: The element of design that describes how a surface feels or appears to feel, such as rough or smooth, is
questions.explanation: Texture is the actual or implied surface quality.

questions.stem: Mixing red and yellow paint gives
questions.explanation: Red + yellow, two primaries, produce the secondary colour orange.

questions.stem: Adding black to a pure hue produces a
questions.explanation: A shade is a hue darkened with black; a tint is lightened with white.

questions.stem: The property of a colour that describes how bright or dull it is, is its
questions.explanation: Intensity (chroma or saturation) is the purity or brightness of a colour.

questions.stem: A painter who wants a very quiet bedroom wall using only light and dark versions of blue is using a
questions.explanation: A monochromatic scheme uses tints, tones and shades of a single hue.

questions.stem: When red is mixed with its complementary colour in equal amounts, the result is
questions.explanation: Complementaries cancel each other's hue, giving a neutral brown-grey.

questions.stem: A painter in a village without shop-bought paints wants a black pigment. The MOST suitable local source is
options: kaolin clay from a stream bank
yellow ochre earth from a road cut
questions.explanation: Charcoal (carbon) gives black; kaolin is white and ochre is yellow-brown.

questions.stem: Dragging a brush that holds very little paint lightly over a rough surface, leaving broken strokes, is
questions.explanation: Dry brush leaves scratchy, broken marks because the paint catches only on raised parts of the surface.

questions.stem: Fresco secco differs from true fresco in that the colours are applied on
questions.explanation: Secco means dry: pigment with a binder is painted on dry plaster; true fresco uses wet plaster.

questions.stem: A painter wants rich, deep colour in a portrait by laying several thin transparent layers over a dry monochrome underpainting. The technique is
questions.explanation: Glazing builds luminous colour through transparent layers over dry paint.

questions.stem: One disadvantage of egg tempera compared with oil paint is that tempera
options: dries too fast for smooth blending
never dries at all, even after months
always turns yellow within a week
must be applied with a knife
questions.explanation: Tempera dries in seconds, so blending is done by hatching rather than smooth wet blending.

questions.stem: A picture made from small cubes of coloured stone or glass, called tesserae, set in cement is a
questions.explanation: Mosaics are built from tesserae.

questions.stem: Applying a thin, semi-opaque broken layer of light colour over a dry darker colour so that the lower colour shows through is
questions.explanation: Scumbling softens and textures a surface with a broken opaque layer.

questions.stem: Spraying as a decorative technique is MOST suitable for
options: painting very fine lines of lettering by hand
questions.explanation: Spray guns and airbrushes give fast, even coverage and smooth gradations.

questions.stem: A large painting on the outside wall of a school showing the history of the community is a
questions.explanation: A mural is painted directly on a wall surface.

questions.stem: In flat painting of a wall, the painter should
options: drag a comb through wet glaze in waves
press crumpled rags into the paint
leave the brush marks deliberately raised
questions.explanation: Flat painting aims at a uniform, smooth single colour.

questions.topic: Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting
questions.stem: A painting of the hills, rivers and trees of the Obudu area is a
questions.explanation: Nature or landscape painting depicts natural scenery.

questions.topic: Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting
questions.stem: An observational painting differs from an imaginative painting because the observational painting is
options: created only from dreams and stories
done from real objects or scenes
questions.explanation: Observational work records what is seen; imaginative work is drawn from memory and fantasy.

questions.topic: Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting
questions.stem: A painting of a seated chief in full regalia, focused on his face and dress, is a
questions.explanation: Portraits and life paintings depict the human figure.

questions.topic: Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting
questions.stem: Paintings that record important events such as a coronation for future generations perform a
questions.explanation: Pictorial painting can document history and preserve culture.

questions.stem: Kaolin (white chalk) is used in some Nigerian ceremonies to
questions.explanation: White clay is applied to the skin in ritual and festival body painting.

questions.stem: Which of these is a MODERN material for body decoration?
questions.explanation: Commercial cosmetics are modern; camwood, kaolin, uli and charcoal are traditional.

questions.stem: Black eye-liner made traditionally from powdered antimony ore and used by many Hausa and Yoruba women is
questions.explanation: Tiro (kohl/antimony) darkens the eyelids and lashes for beauty.

questions.stem: One important SOCIAL function of traditional body decoration is to
options: protect skin from cuts and insect bites
questions.explanation: Designs often signal identity, status, initiation or celebration.

questions.stem: Which of these is a MODERN material used to decorate interior walls?
questions.explanation: Emulsion paint is a modern decorative finish; the others are traditional.

questions.stem: Repeating diamond, zigzag and triangle shapes along the base of a wall is the use of
questions.explanation: Geometric shapes repeated form patterns typical of wall decoration.

questions.stem: One difference between traditional and modern wall decoration is that traditional wall decoration
options: is always done with spray guns
questions.explanation: Traditional wall art uses earth pigments and is part of community life; modern decoration uses factory products.

questions.stem: Washable gloss or satin finishes are preferred on the walls of a hospital corridor mainly because they
options: are cheaper than all other paints
questions.explanation: Smooth, washable finishes allow frequent cleaning.

questions.stem: In a perspective drawing, the horizon line represents the
questions.explanation: The horizon line is at the viewer's eye level.

questions.stem: Two telephone poles of the same height are painted, one far away and one near. To show depth, the far pole should be
questions.explanation: Diminishing size and position nearer the horizon show distance.

questions.stem: Drawing an arm pointing straight at the viewer so that it appears shortened is called
questions.explanation: Foreshortening shortens forms receding from the viewer.

questions.stem: Which career is directly linked to pictorial painting?
questions.explanation: Illustrators create pictures for books, magazines and media.

questions.stem: Painting and decorating contributes to the economy MAINLY by
questions.explanation: The trade employs painters, suppliers and dealers and brings income.

questions.stem: A wall measures 4.5 m by 2.8 m. At ₦7,500 per square metre for labour, the labour charge is
A room has 48 m² of wall to receive two coats of emulsion. If 1 litre covers 12 m² per coat, the paint needed is
questions.explanation: Total area painted = 2 x 48 = 96 m²; 96/12 = 8 litres.

questions.stem: Before an exhibition opens to the public, invited guests, critics and buyers are often shown the works at a
questions.explanation: A preview or private view lets invited guests see and reserve works before the public opening.

questions.stem: A gallery sells a painting for ₦250,000 and keeps a 30% commission. The artist receives
questions.explanation: 30% of 250,000 = 75,000 commission; artist gets 175,000.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between pictorial and decorative painting. [4 marks]
(b) List four tools or equipment used in pictorial painting and state the use of each. [8 marks]
(c) Name three principles of design. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) pictorial: expresses ideas or represents subjects on canvas/paper for viewing
2 marks: (a) decorative: beautifies surfaces such as walls, objects and bodies
8 marks: (b) any four with use: easel (holds canvas), palette (mixing), brushes (applying paint), palette knife (mixing/impasto), canvas/stretcher (support), mahl stick (steadying hand) (2 each)
3 marks: (c) any three: balance, rhythm, emphasis/dominance, proportion, harmony, contrast, unity (1 each)
questions.explanation: Pictorial painting represents ideas; decorative painting beautifies surfaces. Tools: easel, palette, brushes, palette knife, canvas. Principles: balance, rhythm, emphasis, proportion, harmony.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following properties of colour: hue, tone and intensity. [6 marks]
(b) Describe analogous and complementary colour schemes, giving one example of each. [6 marks]
(c) Name three local sources of colour in Nigeria and the colour obtained from each. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) hue: the name of the colour, e.g. red
2 marks: (a) tone (value): lightness or darkness of a colour
2 marks: (a) intensity: brightness or dullness/purity of a colour
3 marks: (b) analogous: colours next to each other on the wheel, e.g. yellow, yellow-orange, orange
3 marks: (b) complementary: colours opposite on the wheel, e.g. red and green / blue and orange
3 marks: (c) any three: camwood–red, kaolin–white, charcoal–black, indigo–blue, laterite/ochre–brown/yellow, henna–reddish-brown (1 each)
questions.explanation: Hue is the colour name, tone its lightness, intensity its brightness. Analogous colours are neighbours; complementaries are opposites. Local: camwood red, kaolin white, charcoal black, indigo blue.

questions.stem: Describe each of the following decorative painting techniques and state one tool or material used: (a) rag rolling [3 marks] (b) combing [3 marks] (c) spraying [3 marks] (d) mosaic [3 marks] (e) mural [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) rag rolling: rolling a twisted rag over a wet glaze to lift or apply paint, giving a broken pattern; rag/cloth, glaze
3 marks: (b) combing: dragging a toothed comb through wet glaze to make lines or wavy patterns; rubber/steel comb
3 marks: (c) spraying: atomising paint onto a surface for even coverage; spray gun/airbrush, compressor
3 marks: (d) mosaic: setting small coloured pieces (tesserae) in cement or adhesive to form a design; glass, tiles, stones
3 marks: (e) mural: large painting directly on wall or ceiling; brushes, emulsion/acrylic paints, scaffold
questions.explanation: Rag rolling uses a rag over glaze; combing uses a comb through glaze; spraying uses a spray gun; mosaic uses tesserae; murals are large wall paintings with brushes and acrylics.

questions.stem:
(a) What is meant by interior decoration? [2 marks]
(b) A family in Kano wants to know how their grandmother's decorated mud walls differ from the painted walls of their new house. Give three differences. [6 marks]
(c) List four materials for modern wall decoration. [4 marks]
(d) State three functions of wall decoration. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) beautifying the inside of a building using paints, wall coverings and designs
6 marks: (b) any three: traditional uses local pigments vs modern factory paints; traditional by community/women vs professionals; traditional has cultural/symbolic motifs vs modern for style/fashion; traditional less durable vs modern washable (2 each)
4 marks: (c) any four: emulsion paint, gloss paint, wallpaper, PVC panels, tiles, textured coatings, stencil paints (1 each)
3 marks: (d) any three: beautification, protection of wall surface, cultural expression, hygiene, identity/branding (1 each)
questions.explanation: Interior decoration beautifies interiors. Traditional work uses local pigments and symbols; modern uses factory products. Materials: emulsion, gloss, wallpaper, tiles. Functions: beauty, protection, culture, hygiene.

questions.stem:
A decorator is to paint a mural 7 m long and 3.2 m high in a hotel lobby in Calabar. Materials: acrylic paints ₦48,000, brushes and rollers ₦9,500, primer ₦15,500, scaffold hire ₦4,000 per day for 6 days. Labour is ₦6,500 per square metre.
(a) Calculate the area of the mural. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the total cost of materials and scaffold hire. [4 marks]
(c) Calculate the labour charge. [2 marks]
(d) If 15% is added to the total cost for profit, calculate the price to quote. [4 marks]
(e) State three other factors that may affect the price. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) area = 7 x 3.2 = 22.4 m²
2 marks: (b) scaffold = 4,000 x 6 = ₦24,000
2 marks: (b) materials + scaffold = 48,000 + 9,500 + 15,500 + 24,000 = ₦97,000
2 marks: (c) labour = 22.4 x 6,500 = ₦145,600
2 marks: (d) total cost = 97,000 + 145,600 = ₦242,600
2 marks: (d) price = 242,600 x 1.15 = ₦278,990
3 marks: (e) any three: location/height of wall, time required, complexity/quality of design, artist reputation, transport (1 each)
questions.explanation: Area 22.4 m²; materials and scaffold ₦97,000; labour ₦145,600; total ₦242,600; quote ₦278,990. Price also depends on location, time, complexity and reputation.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain pricing and negotiation in the marketing of paintings. [4 marks]
(b) Describe four outlets for selling paintings. [8 marks]
(c) State three ways an artist can publicise his or her works. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) pricing: fixing the selling price considering costs, time, demand and reputation
2 marks: (a) negotiation: discussion between artist and buyer to agree an acceptable price
8 marks: (b) any four described: art galleries, exhibitions/art fairs, online platforms/social media, hotels and airports shops, direct commissions, auctions (2 each)
3 marks: (c) any three: social media posts, exhibitions, catalogues/brochures, radio/TV/newspaper, business cards, website (1 each)
questions.explanation: Pricing sets a value; negotiation agrees the final price. Outlets: galleries, exhibitions, online, hotels, commissions, auctions. Publicity: social media, exhibitions, brochures, media.
